MOST of the comments are really helpful. But, if you really did:

I've just about reached the end of puberty

Give it some time. It doesn't matter if it took you 30 years to reach this point. Your body has just finished a huge shift. Things are still crazy inside, but they are starting to settle into their own rhythm. Before you get down on your beard, or start trying to find ways to bolster it... just give it a chance. I know when my shit started to calm down after puberty. not all that long ago when I think about it, I couldn't get a real 5 o'clock shadow. But, as time goes your beard settles into a system. Then you can worry about making it look more full, or styling it.

TL;DR: Give it some time. Play with its natural growth and style. Then slowly (SLOWLY) start playing with different grooming and styling techniques. Don't rush the beard. It will happen in its own glorious way, at its own glorious time.

Most men can't grow a full beard until their late 20s. So you've got some time to go yet. My recommendation is to shave, then wait a couple of days. That won't actually make your beard grow faster, incidentally, that's a thoroughly discredited myth. What this will do is help you figure out where your beard is coming in, so you can plan your style accordingly. Most men can grow a soul patch--you might start there. You might also consider some beard alternatives until your beard fully develops. You can't go wrong with a neatly trimmed mustache. Or even a full Nietzsche if you think you can pull it off. Avoid the Chaplin, though. It's not a good look on anyone. I'd also avoid mutton chops, but hey, it's your face.

edit: Also, if I may put forward a slice of personal philosophy, don't shape your mustache with products, like wax. It'll make you look like a frivolous, vain man with not enough important things to do. Shape by shaving and trimming only.

What kind of games you like the most?

I suppose this isn't limited only to indie games, but I like games that don't battle for control with me as a player. In other words, I like games that allow me as much agency as possible. So for example, I really don't care for unnecessary cut scenes. In fact, I believe that designers/writers should try to make their games with as close to zero cut scenes in the game as possible. I always believe if you're going to take away control from me as a player, it should be meaningful. To give an example, if I can't control my character, then it should probably mean that the player character is bound or can't move for some reason. Sometimes I feel like some developers would be better off making a movie than a game.
Depends on my overall mood. Lately, I've been into build and survive games. Ark and Don't Starve are the big two I'm playing. Also Dying Light ATM.

I really connect to inventory in a game. This usually puts me in a party based RPG range from old final fantasy, to KOTOR 1 and 2, to pirate and space trading sims. I like an economy to manage, and a lot of things to buy. This is one aspect I like in most MMORPGs, but it seems there's often a lot of inventory I can't use. Interestingly, RTS games scratch this itch for me in a way I can't describe.

I prefer sandbox games. The games I've put the most hours in (and currently play every other day) are Minecraft (modded) and Terraria. I also recently bought ARK: Survival and have been enjoying that as well.
